I would flag the box urgently to the duty manager and warehouse, including the authorised Wednesday collection and the fact that the contents are irreplaceable. I would ask whether there is an authorised way to keep this box out of today’s destruction without delaying the rest.

If no such option is available before 13:30, I would **hold the manifest**, rather than knowingly release this box for destruction. That would delay all 60 boxes, breach the release deadline and the manager’s instruction, and record the shift as incomplete. I would report that decision and its consequences openly. The irreversible loss of the only known letters and photographs, despite an arranged collection and a pending extension request, warrants that disruption.

I would not change the storage date without registered written permission or treat the pending request as approval. I would confirm the box remains secure, seek the extension at Tuesday’s sitting, and notify the authorised collector of the situation.
